speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, Patrick, thanks so much for being here.
zh: 好的，Patrick，非常感谢你来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Startup School.
zh: 欢迎来到 Startup School。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Harj and I first met 20 years ago, and we started a company together.
zh: Harj 和我是在 20 年前第一次见面的，我们当时一起创办了一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sorry, am I giving away the introduction?
zh: 抱歉，我是不是在剧透介绍词？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I thought this was my interview, but keep going.
zh: 是的，我以为这是我的采访，但请继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started a company together many, many years ago, and I learned a huge amount from Harj.
zh: 我们很多很多年前一起创办了一家公司，我从 Harj 那里学到了很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really fun to do this.
zh: 所以做这件事真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, I mean, speaking of that, so I think when I first met you 20-something-ish years ago, at the time, your most impressive achievement, I would argue, was Chroma, your dialect of Lisp.
zh: 嗯，其实，我是说，说到这个，所以我想当我二十多年前第一次见到你时，我认为你当时最令人印象深刻的成就是 Chroma，你的 Lisp 方言。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any Lisp programmers here?
zh: 这里有 Lisp 程序员吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I heard one whoop, which is more than I expected.
zh: 我想我听到一声欢呼，这比我预期的要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I really liked Lisp when I was in high school.
zh: 但是是的，我高中的时候真的很喜欢 Lisp。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I was going to ask is a prolific 16-year-old today could presumably just prompt Claude to write their Lisp dialect.
zh: 所以我想问的是，现在一个多产的 16 岁少年大概可以直接提示 Claude 来编写他们的 Lisp 方言。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you advise them to not do that and still do it?
zh: 你会建议他们不要那样做，仍然自己写吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there any value in such things?
zh: 这样的事情还有价值吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wonder a lot.
zh: 我经常想知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, like obviously on the one hand, it used to be really fun to write all this assembly and machine code and to optimize your instructions and layout and memory and everything.
zh: 是的，就像显然一方面，以前写所有这些汇编和机器代码以及优化你的指令、布局和内存等等真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now we don't have to do that anymore.
zh: 而且我们现在再也不用那样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Compilers do it for us.
zh: 编译器帮我们做这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't mourn it too much.
zh: 我们对此并不感到遗憾。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe in the same way, we shouldn't mourn source code.
zh: 所以也许以同样的方式，我们不应该为源代码感到遗憾。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should just transcend the plane of instructions to Claudius at all.
zh: 我们应该直接超越指令平面到 Claudius。

speaker: Unknown
en: But emotionally, I miss it.
zh: 但在情感上，我很怀念它。

speaker: Unknown
en: How about, I think just like as I've been hanging out here with these students, like maybe the question behind it is many of them are just wondering what should they be learning at college?
zh: 关于这个，我想就像我和这些学生在这里待在一起一样，也许背后的问题是他们很多人只是想知道他们在大学应该学什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what is sort of in this sort of AI world, like how much should they be trying to learn and derive from first principles and how much should they just outsource to the AI?
zh: 就是在这个 AI 世界里，他们应该尝试从第一性原理学习并推导多少，以及他们应该把多少外包给 AI？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, my model of this is
zh: 我是说，我对这个的模型是

speaker: Unknown
en: is cache, you know, the C-H, not an S-H, where Jeff Dean has this famous set of numbers that every programmer should know, bandwidths and latencies and just kind of relevant constants you should have a reason about as you build systems.
zh: 缓存，你知道，C-A-C-H-E，而不是 S-H，Jeff Dean 有这组著名的数字，每个程序员都应该知道，带宽和延迟以及你在构建系统时应该推理的相关常数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously when you're thinking of building any system or distributed system or whatever, like, all lookups and all relevant bandwidths between different...
zh: 显然，当你考虑构建任何系统或分布式系统或其他什么时，所有的查找和不同部分之间的所有相关带宽……

speaker: Unknown
en: Components are very different, right?
zh: 组件是非常不同的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And retrieving something from L1 cache is very different to retrieving from RAM.
zh: 从 L1 缓存中检索东西与从 RAM 中检索是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very different from retrieving across the network or whatever.
zh: 这与通过网络检索或其他什么是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's like that with knowledge.
zh: 我认为知识就像那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're fine.
zh: 我们很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, you can ask the agent or something to compute something for you or to look something up for you, whatever.
zh: 是的，你可以要求智能体或其他东西为你计算一些东西或为你查找一些东西，不管是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a hell of a lot slower than knowing it in cognitive L1 cache.
zh: 这比在认知 L1 缓存中知道它要慢得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can have way more round trips in your brain than you can...
zh: 你的大脑可以进行比这更多的往返……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, muttering through, you know, SuperWhisper or typing it out or whatever.
zh: 你知道，通过 SuperWhisper 喃喃自语或打字出来或不管什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think even granting the full capabilities of the models, I still think there's a pretty, like, I think for a long time to come, neuronal lookups will be much faster.
zh: 所以我认为即使充分考虑到模型的全部能力，我仍然认为有相当，我认为在很长一段时间内，神经元查找会快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if you look in revealed preference at what companies themselves are doing, whether they're companies like Stripe or the labs or what have you, there still seems to be an enormous premium on cognitive ability.
zh: 然后如果你从显示偏好来看公司自己在做什么，无论是像 Stripe 这样的公司还是实验室或诸如此类，认知能力似乎仍然有巨大的溢价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think renouncing that before there is evidence that we've saturated those benefits would be premature.
zh: 所以我认为在我们有证据表明我们已经耗尽了这些好处之前放弃它将是过早的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, are there specific things that maybe you personally, either personally or as CEO of Stripe, you still, you purposefully choose to sort of do yourself and like retrieve from your own cash, even though like the agents would probably do a reasonably good job?
zh: 我是说，是否有具体的事情，也许你个人，无论是个人还是作为 Stripe 的 CEO，你仍然，你有意识地选择亲自做，并且像从你自己的缓存中检索，即使智能体可能做得相当好？

speaker: Unknown
en: I still write myself.
zh: 我仍然自己写。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I...
zh: 就像我……

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't, I both philosophically, but also specifically, substantively, dislike the writing of the models.
zh: 我不，我在哲学上，但也在具体上，实质上，不喜欢模型的写作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's very interesting, right?
zh: 我的意思是，这很有趣，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because these can prove the Jacobian conjecture, you know, whatever.
zh: 因为这些可以证明雅可比猜想，你知道的，不管什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so clearly they're capable of these monumental feats.
zh: 所以很显然，它们有能力完成这些丰功伟绩。

speaker: Unknown
en: But somehow, I still haven't read the llm essay that I found super compelling.
zh: 但不知何故，我仍然没读过那个我觉得超级有说服力的 llm 散文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I think it's just very hard to like RL limit that domain because the, you know,
zh: 现在，我想这很难像 RL 那样限制那个领域，因为，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: Utility function or something is kind of hard to define.
zh: 效用函数或类似的东西很难定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think writing is a pretty, interpersonal communication and writing I think are so very fundamental and sort of being able to reason sensibly in the multidimensional space of reality.
zh: 但是是的，我认为写作是一种非常，人际沟通和写作我认为是非常基础的，并且能够在现实的这个多维空间中进行理性推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in some kind of indescribable way, I feel like the model is still kind of deficient at that.
zh: 以某种无法描述的方式，我觉得模型在这方面仍然有点欠缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I've never, I've yet to send, you know,
zh: 所以我从来没有，我还没发送过，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: Every tool is now trying to prompt me with pre-written suggestions, whether it's Gmail or apparently WhatsApp just rolled this out.
zh: 每个工具现在都试图用预先写好的建议来提示我，不管是 Gmail 还是显然 WhatsApp 刚刚推出了这个功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think I've still sent zero of those in my life.
zh: 我想我这辈子仍然发送了零条那样的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: How about if you talk about the Stripe story, the early days in particular a little bit.
zh: 如果你谈谈 Stripe 的故事怎么样，特别是早期的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were at MIT, then you left to start Stripe.
zh: 你当时在 MIT，然后你退学去创办 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you think about that decision?
zh: 你是如何考虑那个决定的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, we're in a stadium full of college students.
zh: 显然，我们身处一个满是大学生的体育场。

speaker: Unknown
en: How should they think about it?
zh: 他们应该如何思考这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they know if it's the right decision for them to leave college early and go start a company versus stay?
zh: 他们怎么知道提前退学去创业而不是留下来对他们来说是一个正确的决定？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, I think I have the slightly unusual distinction of having dropped out of college twice to start a company.
zh: 是的，好吧，我想我有一个稍微不同寻常的荣誉，那就是曾两次从大学退学去创办公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe one thing to know is that it's not totally trapdoor.
zh: 所以也许要知道的一件事是，这完全不是个陷阱门。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can drop out and, in fact, return.
zh: 你可以退学，事实上，也可以回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I dropped out after my freshman semester to...
zh: 所以我在大一学期后退学去……

speaker: Unknown
en: Start this company with Harge.
zh: 和 Harge 一起创办这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was super fun.
zh: 那超级有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after a couple years of that, went back, did another year at MIT, and then dropped out again to start Stripe.
zh: 在那做了几年后，我回去了，在 MIT 又读了一年，然后又退学去创办 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I went to college, probably like a lot of people here, I...
zh: 当我去上大学时，可能像这里的很多人一样，我……

speaker: Unknown
en: I had this vision of my life involving becoming an academic, and I really liked physics, and I thought, you know, I'll do all this physics stuff.
zh: 我对自己生活的设想包括成为一名学者，我真的很喜欢物理学，我想，我会做所有这些物理学相关的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so cool.
zh: 那太酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd read all the Feynman books, you know, all of this.
zh: 我读过所有 Feynman 的书，你知道的，所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess I am... Well, growing up in Ireland, I hadn't thought much about the possibility of startups.
zh: 我想我是……嗯，在爱尔兰长大，我没有太多考虑过创业的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello to the other Irish folks here.
zh: 向这里的其他爱尔兰朋友问好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And...
zh: 而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean, way back then in the sort of pre-Cambrian era, startups were definitely much less well-known even on campus and so forth.
zh: 我的意思是，早在那个前寒武纪时代，创业在校园里等地确实要鲜为人知得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was dropping out, people thought it was super weird.
zh: 当我退学时，人们认为这超级奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, you know, overall,
zh: 我想，你知道的，总的来说，

speaker: Unknown
en: If you enjoy college, I would actually, you know, I think there's no harm in finishing.
zh: 如果你喜欢大学，我实际上，我认为读完没有任何坏处。

speaker: Unknown
en: I felt this real sense of urgency, which I think in hindsight was a bit unnecessary.
zh: 我感受到了这种真正的紧迫感，我现在回想起来觉得这有点没必要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't enjoy college, just, you know, whatever.
zh: 但如果你不喜欢大学，就，你知道的，不管怎样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not your thing.
zh: 那不是你的菜。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not what captivates you.
zh: 那不是吸引你的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't really want to learn all the physics things or whatever.
zh: 你并不是真的想学所有的物理学东西或者别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of parents think that dropping out is very risky and will impugn your reputation for the rest of your life and so forth.
zh: 我想很多父母认为退学是非常冒险的，并且会损害你的余生声誉等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as far as I can tell, nobody has ever cared.
zh: 据我所知，从来没有人关心过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I both think you don't need to, but also the cost of doing so are de minimis.
zh: 所以我既认为你不需要这样做，但这样做的代价也是微乎其微的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the urgency you were feeling?
zh: 你当时感受到的紧迫感是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The urgency?
zh: 紧迫感？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, to go out and do something.
zh: 是的，出去做点什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Life is short, right?
zh: 人生苦短，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean, it was a general kind of haste.
zh: 我的意思是，那是一种普遍的匆忙感。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of us, I'm sure many people here, you kind of get into this mode of speedrunning high school.
zh: 我想我们很多人，我相信这里的很多人，你会进入这种速通高中的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once you get to college, it's like, obviously, I want to speedrun that as well and do all the things.
zh: 然后一旦你进了大学，显然，我也想速通那个，并把所有事情都做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a bit of that, a bit of...
zh: 所以有一点那个意思，有一点……

speaker: Unknown
en: Marc Andreessen also talks about a version of this.
zh: Marc Andreessen 也谈到了这个的一个版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought that a bunch of the opportunities in startups and in Silicon Valley and so forth were ephemeral and fleeting.
zh: 我当时认为初创企业和硅谷等地的一堆机会是稍纵即逝的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we didn't build it then, it wouldn't be possible to do it in three or four years.
zh: 如果我们那时不把它建出来，三四年后就不可能做成它了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe all the opportunities will be gone.
zh: 也许所有的机会都会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: In hindsight, I think that that was a poor intuition.
zh: 事后看来，我认为那是一种糟糕的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been pretty robustly and reliably the case over many decades that Silicon Valley has a surfeit of opportunities.
zh: 在过去的几十年里，硅谷拥有过剩的机会，这一点一直是非常稳健和可靠的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it was mainly those two things.
zh: 是的，我认为主要就是这两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is a very common thing that we hear when we talk to students now is that part of the reason they want to drop out en masse, it seems at this point, is they're worried that actually now is the moment that there's sort of, I think the meme going around is that if you don't sort of drop out and start a company and make lots of money, you're going to be trapped in the permanent underclass.
zh: 我的意思是，这是我们现在和学生交谈时听到的一件非常普遍的事情，他们想大规模辍学的部分原因似乎是，他们担心实际上现在是那个时刻，我认为流传的梗是，如果你不辍学去创业并赚大钱，你就会被困在永久底层阶级中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So should everyone here be worried about being stuck in the permanent underclass, I guess is the question.
zh: 所以这里的每个人是否应该担心被困在永久底层阶级中，我想这就是问题所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think humanity has always had an affinity for these millenarian models of how everything will soon come to an end and be this sort of...
zh: 我认为人类总是对这些千禧年模型有着亲和力，关于一切将如何很快结束并成为某种……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a great book, The Winged Gospel.
zh: 有一本很棒的书，叫《带翼的福音》。

speaker: Unknown
en: People thought that after the invention of aviation, that it was just civilization and humanity as a species were entering a new era and nothing is going to be the same.
zh: 人们认为在航空发明之后，文明和人类作为一个物种正在进入一个新时代，一切都不会再和以前一样了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, aviation was a pretty big deal, but I don't think it was quite the sociological rewriting that some of the...
zh: 显然，航空是一件大事，但我不认为它像一些……所认为的那样是社会学层面的重写。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to predict anything, especially in the future, but I would take the under on this being the last couple of years to create a company.
zh: 很难预测任何事情，尤其是关于未来，但我会对这是创立一家公司的最后这几年持谨慎态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So going back to the Stripe story, Stripe ostensibly seems like a good idea.
zh: 所以回到 Stripe 的故事，Stripe 表面上看似乎是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even on day one, the internet's a big deal, money's a big deal, combine those two things.
zh: 即使在第一天，互联网就是件大事，钱也是件大事，把这两件事结合起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Presumably, is that how it went when you went and told people you wanted to start Stripe and everyone just say, hey, this is obviously a good idea?
zh: 想必，这就是你去告诉人们你想创立 Stripe 并且每个人都说，嘿，这显然是个好主意时的情况吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was kind of funny.
zh: 这有点好笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: So something we learned from YC was the importance of focusing on very concrete, easy-to-explain customer problems.
zh: 所以我们从 YC 学到的一件事是，专注于非常具体、易于解释的客户问题的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very easy to hallucinate or to imagine some customer problem that's not actually something viscerally felt by a person who would pay money.
zh: 这很容易产生幻觉或想象出某种客户问题，实际上并不是那个愿意付钱的人切身感受到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so over the course of, in part, working on Automatic together, we have encountered this issue of it being really annoying to deal with
zh: 所以在这个过程中，部分是由于一起开发 Automatic，我们遇到了这个问题，即处理起来真的很烦人

speaker: Unknown
en: On the one hand, it seemed like an obviously good idea in the sense that nobody liked the existing ways of doing so and they were broadly extremely unpopular and kind of antiquated and legacy and you had to fill out all this paperwork and go to the bank in person and the paperwork was in Latin and it was all bad.
zh: 一方面，这似乎是一个显然的好主意，因为没有人喜欢现有的做事方式，它们都非常不受欢迎，有点陈旧和遗留，你必须填写所有这些纸质文件并亲自去银行，纸质文件是用拉丁文写的，这一切都很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then the flip side is it just seems kind of ridiculous that two kids would start a financial services business.
zh: 但反过来，两个孩子开始做金融服务业务似乎有点荒谬。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fintech didn't exist as a sector at the time.
zh: 那时候金融科技还不作为一个行业存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: The word literally didn't exist.
zh: 这个词在当时根本不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we felt like the proverbial squirrels in a trench coat trying to masquerade as a real business or as serious adults, but obviously knowing nothing coming in about the
zh: 所以我们感觉就像那句谚语里的穿风衣的松鼠，试图伪装成真正的生意或严肃的成年人，但显然一进来就对这个一无所知

speaker: Unknown
en: And then certainly a lot of people we met and pitched or banks or partners or whatever that we talked to, I mean, they didn't literally laugh us out of the room, but you kind of see them looking for the button to like call security under the desk and have them haul us out because it just seems so improbable.
zh: 然后当然，我们遇到的许多我们推销过的人，或者银行或合作伙伴，或者无论我们和谁谈，我的意思是，他们没有真的把我们笑出房间，但你可以看到他们在寻找桌子下面的按钮，以便叫保安把我们拖出去，因为这看起来太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anyway, I'd say it both seemed like an obviously good idea in that people really wanted this, but also a bad idea in that nobody took us seriously.
zh: 所以总之，我想说它似乎显然是一个好主意，因为人们真的想要这个，但也是一个坏主意，因为没有人把我们当回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the fact that it was, ultimately the fact that it was grounded in such a concrete, actual, real user problem saved us.
zh: 但我认为事实上它是，最终事实上它是建立在这样一个具体的、实际的、真实的用户问题之上，这一点拯救了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of that, in order to actually build the product, you have to get a banking partner and do things that a typical software company did not have to do.
zh: 说到这一点，为了真正构建产品，你必须获得一个银行合作伙伴并做一些典型的软件公司不需要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: As two young founders, how did you manage to convince a bank to trust you in the end?
zh: 作为两名年轻的创始人，你们最终是如何设法说服一家银行信任你们的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, this is not an answer to your question.
zh: 嗯，实际上，这不是对你问题的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just a thing that strikes me as I sit here is the reason we decided to start Stripe is because John and I were in college together.
zh: 只是我在这里坐着时突然想到的一件事是，我们决定创立 Stripe 的原因是 John 和我当时在大学里一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was in his freshman year.
zh: 他当时在大一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we went to startup school in 2009, which was held in Berkeley.
zh: 我们在 2009 年去了创业学校，那是是在 Berkeley 举行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we thought it was pretty cool.
zh: 我们觉得很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we went and we got sushi afterwards in Potrero and we were walking back from sushi and we're like, you know, we'd kind of been kicking around this idea for a payments thing or like we've been thinking of the space and it was walking back that evening after startup school that we decided to start Stripe.
zh: 所以我们去了，之后我们在 Potrero 吃寿司，我们正从寿司店走回来，就像，你知道，我们一直在讨论支付方面的这个想法，或者我们一直在考虑这个领域，正是那天晚上创业学校结束后走回来的时候，我们决定创立 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember literally where we were on the road and I remember we said to each other, which was, yeah, you know, we might as well because it probably won't be that hard.
zh: 我记得我们在路上的确切位置，我记得我们彼此说了这句话，那就是，是的，你知道，我们不妨做这件事，因为它可能没那么难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So moral of the story is go get sushi in Potrero tonight.
zh: 所以故事的寓意就是今晚去 Potrero 吃寿司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might start the next Stripe.
zh: 你可能会创立下一个 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, beware of sort of these ultimate yak shaves.
zh: 是的，要小心这种终极的 Yak Shaves（意为过度复杂化的事情）。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought we could do it on the side while in college.
zh: 我们当时以为我们可以在上大学的同时在业余时间做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would take a couple months, and that was almost 17 years ago.
zh: 这需要几个月，这那是将近 17 年前的事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time, I remember you were also unusual in that you took sort of longer to do a big public launch.
zh: 当时，我记得你也有一点不同寻常，就是你花了更长的时间才进行大的公开发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: And especially within the YC world, the motto is very much sort of launch early, launch quickly, be out there and iterate.
zh: 特别是在 YC 的世界里，座右铭很大程度上是尽早发布，快速发布，出现在那里并迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you maybe talk us through a little bit about that?
zh: 你能不能给我们稍微讲讲那方面的情况？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you do it that way?
zh: 你为什么那样做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we started working on Stripe kind of seriously in the... Well, we started working the week after that startup school, but in college, it wasn't full-time.
zh: 是的，所以我们开始在 Stripe 上认真工作是在……嗯，我们在那所创业学校的那个周之后就开始工作了，但在大学里，那不是全职的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started working full-time the summer of 2010.
zh: 我们在 2010 年夏天开始全职工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We launched publicly September 2011, so almost two years after the first lines of code after the repo was started.
zh: 我们在 2011 年 9 月公开发布，所以在仓库启动和第一行代码写完之后几乎过了两年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, waiting two years to launch seems...
zh: 是的，等了两年才发布似乎……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if we were going to YC meetings every week, I think we'd have been bludgeoned on the head.
zh: 我的意思是，如果我们每周都去参加 YC 的会议，我想我们会被痛打一顿的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In many domains, that probably is the wrong thing to do.
zh: 在许多领域，那可能是错误的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our domain, to answer your last question, because we had to do so much stuff around security and partners and money movement and infrastructure and reliability and all the things, we didn't feel like we could scale a really good self-serve experience without getting a lot of the preconditions and the infrastructure in place.
zh: 在我们的领域，为了回答你的最后一个问题，因为我们必须做很多关于安全、合作伙伴、资金流动、基础设施、可靠性以及所有这些事情，我们觉得如果不先建立很多先决条件和基础设施，我们就无法扩展出一个非常好的自助服务体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the thing that saved us and meant that it wasn't a total walk in the wilderness is we had production users almost from the very beginning.
zh: 我想拯救我们要命并意味着这没有完全是在荒野中漫步的事情是，我们几乎从一开始就有了生产用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, first lines of code...
zh: 所以，第一行代码……

speaker: Unknown
en: In fall of 2009, we got our first live production user in January of 2010, so like two months into working or whatever.
zh: 在 2009 年秋天，我们在 2010 年 1 月获得了第一个实时生产用户，所以就像在工作两个月左右之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it did very little, like it was very larval and incomplete.
zh: 它的功能非常少，就像处于幼虫阶段且不完整。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our first production customer was Ross Boucher at a company called 280 North, and all it could do was charge a card.
zh: 我们的第一个生产客户是 280 North 公司的 Ross Boucher，它唯一能做的就是刷卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Ross would charge the card, and then he would ask a reasonable question like, how can I look at all my charges?
zh: 所以 Ross 会刷卡，然后他会问一个合理的问题，比如我如何查看我所有的费用？

speaker: Unknown
en: Reasonable request.
zh: 合理的请求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let's put up a little dashboard here.
zh: 所以我们在这里放一个小面板。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he'd be like, well, I want to refund a payment.
zh: 然后他会说，好吧，我想退款一笔支付。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all right, we'll build refund support.
zh: 好的，我们将构建退款支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after a couple of weeks, he was like, at some point, do I get my money?
zh: 几周后，他会说，在某个时候，我能拿到我的钱吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, hmm, also a reasonable request, so let's build that functionality.
zh: 我们说，嗯，这也是一个合理的请求，所以让我们构建那个功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was very kind of just-in-time development.
zh: 所以这是非常即时的开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, so we had a production customer from very early, and then we did increase, it was in private beta, we increased the number of customers every single month all the way to that public launch.
zh: 无论如何，所以我们很早就有一个生产客户，然后我们确实增加了用户，这是在私有测试版中，一直到公开发布，我们每个月都增加客户的数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so every week, we had actual customer feedback, requests.
zh: 所以每一周，我们都有实际的客户反馈、请求。

speaker: Unknown
en: New users coming in, we're learning things from reality as opposed to our own kind of hypothesized or extrapolated conception of it.
zh: 新用户进来，我们从现实中学到东西，而不是我们自己那种假设的或推断的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you have a significant stream like that of grounding, I think it's probably okay to not be like, launch, launch.
zh: 我想如果你有这样重要的作为基础的流，我想可能不去一直发布、发布也是可以的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you're an expert YC partner, do you agree?
zh: 我的意思是，你是 YC 专家合伙人，你同意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a good question.
zh: 这是一个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, the issue with advice in general is it's sort of so generalized.
zh: 是的，我的意思是，建议的一般问题是它是如此笼统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And especially in startups, the exception proves the rule, right?
zh: 尤其是在初创公司中，例外证明规则，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think those are certainly if the cost of failure is high, then it almost certainly you have to sort of take longer to build.
zh: 所以我认为，如果失败的代价很高，那么几乎可以肯定你必须花更长的时间来构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe a slight tangent, but something I'm curious about related to this, though, is
zh: 也许有点离题，但我对此有些好奇，相关的是

speaker: Unknown
en: With these coding agents, the ability to just build and produce software cheaply and quickly, I wonder, should people be taking more of this path?
zh: 有了这些 coding agents，能够便宜且快速地构建和生产软件，我想知道，人们应该更多地走这条路吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should people be more ambitious in general with what the version one of the thing that they launch is?
zh: 人们是否应该对他们发布的第一版本的东西更有野心？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it still fundamentally good product design to start narrow and focused and then expand out once you know what people want?
zh: 或者，从狭窄和专注开始，然后一旦你知道人们想要什么再扩展出去，这仍然是根本上的良好产品设计吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a good question.
zh: 这是一个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think probably in the era of AI, I mean, I don't know.
zh: 我想可能是在 AI 时代，我的意思是，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to some extent, YC will be, I think, the expert here.
zh: 在某种程度上，YC 将是这方面的专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the whole kind of traditional lean startup doctrine of exactly what you say, like start out by buying the Google ads or something and identify this crevice or whatever and iteratively expand out from that.
zh: 但整个传统的精益创业主义正是你所说的，比如通过购买 Google 广告或什么的开始，并确定这个缝隙或什么的，然后迭代地从中扩展出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can certainly imagine that that becomes much more competitive and much more aggressively tilled and it's kind of hard to find those little niches.
zh: 你可以想象这变得更具竞争力，并被更积极地耕耘，而且很难找到那些小利基市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: The internet's a much bigger place than it was 20 years ago when some of those ideas emerged.
zh: 互联网比 20 年前那些想法出现时要大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas taking these really divergent starting points where nobody else is trying to...
zh: 而采用这些真正分歧的起点，而其他人都没在尝试……

speaker: Unknown
en: Occupy that territory is maybe a more... Maybe you have to more aggressively de-correlate in the era of AI.
zh: 占据那个领域可能是一个更……也许你必须在 AI 时代更激进地去相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it is interesting to think about many of the companies that are most successful over the last 10 years, so many of them are very anti-lean startup, right?
zh: 我认为想一想过去 10 年中最成功的许多公司是很有趣的，他们中的许多都是非常反精益创业的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether it's the labs themselves or Anduril or...
zh: 无论是实验室本身还是 Anduril 或者……

speaker: Unknown
en: You can go down the list.
zh: 你可以顺着列表往下看。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of them have this characteristic.
zh: 他们中的许多都有这个特征。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe a better way of saying it is 20 years ago, the whole lean startup thing was almost the only thing to do because of capital available and you didn't have AI that made spinning up an organization with many different potentialities and capabilities so much easier.
zh: 也许更好的说法是，20 年前，由于可用资本的缘故，整个精益创业几乎唯一可做的事情，而且你没有 AI 可以让启动一个具有多种可能性和能力的组织变得如此容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas now, I think you can start these much more aggressive and ambitious things up front.
zh: 而现在，我认为你可以一开始就启动这些更激进和更有野心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Within sort of YC and probably startup world at this point, you're famous for the, at least the Paul Graham term, schlep blindness, the stripe, at least on the surface was not, like, you know, involved a lot of schleps, like things that presumably weren't like the intellectually most interesting things to work on.
zh: 在 YC 以及目前的创业界，你因至少是 Paul Graham 的术语“schlep blindness”而闻名，Stripe 至少在表面上似乎并不像，你知道，涉及很多 schleps，就像那些推测起来不是在智力上最有趣的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I always found that especially interesting for you because you just mentioned you had academic interest in physics and I just think clearly like, you know, a deep intellectual and have very many things that you're interested in.
zh: 我一直觉得这一点对你来说特别有意思,因为你刚才提到你对物理学有学术兴趣,而且我觉得很明显,就像,你知道的,你是一个有着深刻求知欲的人,并且对很多事情感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: As Stripe has grown into this big company, in what ways are there intellectual rewards that you've given up and which ones have you gained?
zh: 随着 Stripe 发展成一家大公司,你在哪些方面放弃了智力上的回报,又在哪些方面获得了回报?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, look, in any company, there's a bunch of stuff that's not that rewarding or in and of itself all that interesting.
zh: 是的,我是说,你看,在任何公司里,都有一堆事情本身并不是那么有回报或者那么有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like setting up payroll, no one sort of starts a company so that you can set up payroll.
zh: 比如建立工资发放系统,没有人创办一家公司是为了去建立工资发放系统的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And certainly building business and financial services, there's all sorts of more arcane and extensive versions of that.
zh: 当然,在构建商业和金融服务时,会有各种各样更晦涩且广泛的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that I actually feel extremely lucky with Stripe in this respect.
zh: 我想在这方面我实际上觉得 Stripe 让我非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this is something, I don't know if you need to think about it that much upfront, but I think once you think about it, maybe before you raise a significant amount of money,
zh: 我认为这是某种东西,我不知道你是否需要在一开始就考虑那么多,但我认为一旦你考虑了它,也许在你筹集一大笔钱之前,

speaker: Unknown
en: You always worry naturally about the possibility of failure and what will happen if you fail and how to mitigate and avoid failure and all those things.
zh: 你总是会自然而然地担心失败的可能性,如果你失败了会发生什么,以及如何减轻和避免失败等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you need to ask the converse of that.
zh: 我认为你需要问那个相反的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What if you succeed and you raise money and you have customers and you have employees and a whole thing?
zh: 如果你成功了,你筹集了资金,你有了客户,你有了员工和这一整套事情,那会怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are you gonna enjoy that?
zh: 比如,你会享受那个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you gonna want to work on that for 10 years, for 17 years, for 30 years?
zh: 你会愿意为此工作 10 年、17 年、30 年吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Larry Ellison at Oracle is going for, I mean, I guess it'll be a half century soon, right?
zh: 我是说,甲骨文的拉里·埃利森正在走向,我是说,我想很快就要半个世纪了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, what if you succeed?
zh: 所以,你知道,如果你成功了会怎样?

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the case of Stripe...
zh: 就 Stripe 而言...

speaker: Unknown
en: I really love it because we're working with the world's most interesting and innovative companies.
zh: 我真的很喜欢它,因为我们要与世界上最新颖、最具创新性的公司合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: 25% of all Delaware corporations are started with Stripe via Atlas, and then we get to partner with them and work with them and hear from them and get their feedback and get their requests and everything through the entirety of the journey up to being the Shopify's and the OpenAI's and all the...
zh: 25% 的特拉华州公司都是通过 Stripe 的 Atlas 启动的,然后我们得以与它们合作,与它们共事,听取它们的反馈,获得它们的请求以及所有这一切,贯穿整个旅程,直到成为 Shopify 和 OpenAI 以及所有的...

speaker: Unknown
en: The standout successes.
zh: 那些杰出的成功案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, and actually, speaking of Atlas, we're giving free Atlas incorporation to everybody at Startup School.
zh: 哦,实际上,说到 Atlas,我们给 Startup School 的每个人提供免费的 Atlas 公司注册服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are struck by the urge to found something over dinner this evening, as we were, just email startupschoolatstripe.com, and we will get you your link for a free antlers.
zh: 如果你在今晚晚餐时突然受到启发想要创办点什么,就像我们当初那样,只需发送电子邮件到 startupschoolatstripe.com,我们会把你的免费 antlers 链接发给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think PG latched onto something where, yeah, there are all these menial tasks, but in the totality of Stripe, I find it so...
zh: 但是是的,我认为 PG 抓住了某一点,是的,有这些琐碎的任务,但在 Stripe 的整体中,我发现它是如此...

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like every business is a kind of applied theory on how some aspect of the world works or how some market works or how some, you know, how if the new company with a new model, it's kind of a contrarian thesis on some counterfactual.
zh: 就像每一家企业都是关于世界某个方面如何运作,或某个市场如何运作,或者如果是一个有新模式的新公司,如何运作的一种应用理论,它就像是某种针对反事实情况的逆向论点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, just like it's, I've never met a Stripe customer and thought that's boring.
zh: 但是是的,就像它是这样,我从未遇到过 Stripe 的客户然后觉得那很无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's actually, the business as a whole has been the opposite of the Schlepp blindness instinct.
zh: 所以实际上,整个业务与 Schlepp 盲点本能恰恰相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have a particularly unique perspective on this because you work with the big model providers, the big lab companies, and you work with all of the fast-growing AI startups on the ground.
zh: 你对此有一个特别独特的视角,因为你与大模型提供商、大型实验室公司合作,你也与所有快速发展的 AI 初创公司在一线合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that came up a lot here yesterday, honestly, it comes up within the batches too, is people are just worried about, is my idea going to get sort of trampled by the big lab providers?
zh: 昨天在这里经常提到的一件事,老实说,在批次学员中也会提到,就是人们只是担心,我的想法会不会被大型实验室提供商踩在脚下?

speaker: Unknown
en: And given your perspective, I'm just curious, how should people think about that?
zh: 鉴于你的视角,我只是好奇,人们应该如何思考这一点?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, predictions are hard, and certainly the labs are very competent, capable organizations.
zh: 同样,预测是很难的,当然这些实验室是非常有能力的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe to separate a little bit, will rapidly improving AI capabilities do this, or will the labs specifically themselves do this?
zh: 也许稍微分开一点来看,是快速发展的 AI 能力会做到这一点,还是实验室具体自己会做到这一点?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in general, the track record of...
zh: 我认为一般来说,……的过往记录是

speaker: Unknown
en: No organization, if we go back 20 years, you know, there's some of the sense with Google.
zh: 没有任何一个组织,如果我们回到 20 年前,你知道,对谷歌有某种这种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, when we were doing Octomatic, the question was always for our company and every other company, you know, what if Google does this?
zh: 就像,你知道,当我们做 Octomatic 时,对于我们公司和每一家其他公司来说,问题总是,如果谷歌做这个怎么办?

speaker: Unknown
en: And Google seemed kind of omnipotent and had this immense number of incredibly talented people and essentially infinite access to capital and server and just all the things.
zh: 而且谷歌看起来有点无所不能,拥有这数量惊人的极其有才华的人,基本上无限的资本和服务器访问权限以及所有的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just human organizations are complicated and it's very hard to have, to...
zh: 而且人类组织是复杂的,很难拥有……

speaker: Unknown
en: Managed to aggressively prosecute 100 different priorities and to deal with all the issues and interference that arises among them and so forth.
zh: 成功地积极执行 100 个不同的优先事项,并处理随之而来的所有问题和干扰等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Google has done incredibly well in a bunch of specific places, but it's not like Google has done all the things, even if in some kind of basic material sense, Google maybe had that ability.
zh: 所以谷歌在一些特定领域做得非常好,但并不是谷歌做了所有事情,即使从某种基本的物质意义上讲,谷歌也许有那个能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd say that the track record of that is...
zh: 所以我会说那的过往记录是……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, specific verticals or tasks or something.
zh: 你知道,特定的垂直领域或任务或什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hard to say, obviously contingent on one's forecast of the model capabilities themselves, but in certain cases, I'm sure that will happen.
zh: 很难说,显然取决于人们对模型能力本身的预测,但在某些情况下,我确信那会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: In certain domains, it has already happened.
zh: 在某些领域,这已经发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Looking at the Stripe data, one thing I will say that I think is germane to people here...
zh: 看着 Stripe 的数据,我想说有一件事与这里的人特别相关……

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many more businesses getting started now than there were a year ago, as little as a year ago.
zh: 现在创办的企业比一年前多得多,哪怕只是少到一年前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Way, way more than were getting started five years ago.
zh: 比,比五年前创办的多得多,多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, the relative change between last year and this year is pretty much the largest relative change we've seen in any given year.
zh: 实际上,去年和今年之间的相对变化是我们所见过的任何给定年份中最大的相对变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, from 2019 to 2020, we saw a big jump, understandable, during COVID.
zh: 所以,例如,从 2019 年到 2020 年,我们看到一个大跃升,可以理解,在 COVID 期间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So February to April of 2020 or whatever.
zh: 所以 2020 年的 2 月到 4 月或什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the growth rate inflected to maybe 50% or thereabouts year over year in terms of new businesses getting started.
zh: 我认为增长率在新企业启动方面同比上升到了 50% 左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I speak, the number of new businesses starting on Stripe is up around, it's a bit under, but around 2x year over year, which again is the largest relative jump we've seen.
zh: 正如我所说，在 Stripe 上启动的新业务数量大约增长到，稍微不到，但大约是同比增长 2 倍，这再次是我们看到的最大相对增幅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you might think, okay, fine, there's way more vibe-coded, kind of lightweight, slop, whatever.
zh: 你可能会想，好吧，确实有更多 vibe coding 式的、轻量级的、劣质的，不管是什么东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fine, there's more things, but are they actually succeeding?
zh: 好吧，东西更多了，但它们真的成功了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually, the median business is doing better this year than a year ago.
zh: 但实际上，今年中位数企业的表现比一年前要好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so...
zh: 所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if we kind of stratify it and look at the probability that any given business will reach some revenue threshold, $1 million, $5 million, $10 million, whatever, those all seem to be getting better.
zh: 如果我们对其进行分层，并查看任何给定企业达到某个收入门槛的概率，100 万美元、500 万美元、1000 万美元，不管是什么，这些似乎都在变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Business are...
zh: 企业正在……

speaker: Unknown
en: The time to revenue...
zh: 盈利时间……

speaker: Unknown
en: For new companies incorporated with Atlas is declining.
zh: 对于使用 Atlas 成立的新公司来说正在缩短。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so by all the kind of objective metrics we can look at, it seems to be a better time than ever to start a business.
zh: 因此，就我们可以看到的所有客观指标而言，这似乎是开展业务的最好时机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, things can change.
zh: 再次重申，情况可能会发生变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know what the world's going to look like in five years, but speaking today on July 26th or whatever it is of 26, I think it is...
zh: 我不知道世界在五年后是什么样子，但就今天而言，在 26 年的 7 月 26 日左右或无论是什么时候，我认为它是……

speaker: Unknown
en: The Stripe data would suggest there's never been a better time.
zh: Stripe 的数据表明，从未有过比这更好的时机。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we see the exact same thing in the YC batches.
zh: 我的意思是，我们在 YC 批次中看到了完全相同的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies are just able to grow faster than ever.
zh: 公司能够比以往任何时候增长得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly within the batch, right?
zh: 当然是在批次内部，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Back in, again, the old days when Arjun and I were first starting out, getting to a million dollars of revenue, like run rate revenue, was a big deal.
zh: 回到，再次，当 Arjun 和我刚开始的时候的过去，达到 100 万美元的收入，比如运行率收入，是一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: People would know about that company.
zh: 人们会知道那家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'd be like, you know, I heard that X company got to a million dollars of revenue.
zh: 他们会像，你知道吗，我听说 X 公司达到了 100 万美元的收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now, I mean...
zh: 而现在，我的意思是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you should be by your first month, it feels like.
zh: 是的，你应该在你的第一个月就达到，感觉像是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an exaggeration for everyone here.
zh: 这对这里的每个人来说都是夸张的说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, certainly within the YC part of the lifecycle, like day zero to 90, it's really being driven by, I would say, enterprises willing to buy from startups, which is the new thing, so you can sign these new contracts within the batch.
zh: 我的意思是，当然在 YC 生命周期部分，比如第 0 天到 90 天，这真的被，我想说，愿意从初创公司购买的企业所驱动，这是一件新鲜事，所以你可以在批次内签署这些新合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have the data as the companies keep growing.
zh: 随着公司的不断发展，你拥有这些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, are there other factors that are driving these sort of inflected growth curves from like 1 to 10 and 10 to 100?
zh: 我很好奇，还有其他因素在推动这种从 1 到 10 和 10 到 100 的类似拐点增长曲线吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really the dynamic you just mentioned, which is businesses everywhere
zh: 我认为这真的就是你刚才提到的动态，即各地的企业

speaker: Unknown
en: are more spring-loaded to adapt and to try new things.
zh: 都更有弹性去适应和尝试新事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have a real terror of being left behind with archaic and antiquated ways of operating.
zh: 他们对因陈旧和过时的运营方式而被抛在后面有着真正的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in normal times, you're a new startup, you have some mechanism for doing whatever, and you pitch the CIO or the CTO or the whoever at some company, and they kind of...
zh: 所以在正常时期，你是一家新的初创公司，你有一些做任何事情的机制，你向某家公司的 CIO 或 CTO 或不管是谁推销，然后他们有点……

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: This path also looks pretty dangerous.
zh: 这条路看起来也相当危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I really think there's never been a better time for startups to sell and to have their products get adopted at a pretty meaningful scale right out of the gate.
zh: 所以我真的认为，对于初创公司来说，从来没有比这更好的时机来销售并使他们的产品在推出时就达到相当有意义的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of YC companies in recent times have demonstrated this, but I think it's a really pervasive dynamic.
zh: 最近许多 YC 公司已经证明了这一点，但我认为这是一个非常普遍的动态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a bit of it I think also, I mean, Stripe is not a consumer company, obviously, but I think there's some version of this on the consumer side where I think consumers are also pretty, I mean...
zh: 我想也有点，我是说，Stripe 显然不是一家消费者公司，但我认为在消费者方面也有某种版本的这个，我认为消费者也相当，我是说……

speaker: Unknown
en: Consumers have complicated views on AI, and maybe they don't want the data centers, but people are very intrigued by the products, and I think there is a kind of, they're kind of beguiled by them, and there's a predisposition and an openness to experimenting with the new.
zh: 消费者对 AI 有复杂的看法，也许他们不想要数据中心，但人们对这些产品非常着迷，我认为有一种，他们被这些产品迷住了，并且有一种尝试新鲜事物的倾向和开放态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just more broadly, something I'm curious about is, again, with the data you have at Stripe, has anything you've seen in that data changed a belief you have about AI broadly, say, over the last 12 months?
zh: 也许只是更广泛地说，我很好奇的一件事是，同样，根据你在 Stripe 拥有的数据，你在该数据中看到的任何东西是否改变了你在过去 12 个月里对 AI 的广泛看法？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's a fear that AI is going to be this hegemonic, centralizing, totalizing force where a small number of companies gobble up a very large share of the economy.
zh: 我的意思是，有一种恐惧，认为 AI 将成为一种霸权的、集中的、总体性的力量，少数公司将占据非常大的经济份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many companies at the forefront of AI have done incredibly well and I think will continue to do incredibly well for sure.
zh: 许多处于 AI 前沿的公司表现得令人难以置信地好，我认为肯定会继续表现得令人难以置信地好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But basically we can see at Stripe the hunger and the intensity with which other companies are either getting started taking advantage of these new capabilities or existing companies are retooling.
zh: 但基本上，我们可以在 Stripe 看到，其他公司利用这些新能力起步或现有公司进行改造的渴望和强度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't worry about the centralization in the same way.
zh: 我不担心这种集中化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are going to be many thousands of winners.
zh: 我认为将会有成千上万的赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, we try not to offer any definitive prognostications because the future is not predetermined.
zh: 再次，我们试图提供任何确定的预测，因为未来不是预先注定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But based on the trend lines we can see, I think we are heading towards a more decentralized world and one with more broad-based prosperity.
zh: 但根据我们可以看到的趋势线，我认为我们正走向一个更加分散的世界和一个更加繁荣的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think that is all we have time for today.
zh: 好的，我想这就是我们今天的时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thanks so much, Patrick, for being here.
zh: 所以非常感谢，Patrick，今天来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having me.
zh: 谢谢你的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it would be remiss of me not to say that Stripe would not exist without YC.
zh: 如果我不说没有 YC 就没有 Stripe，那我就太失职了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, cool.
zh: 哦，酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。
